Q3: I use it for most things in the research process other than peer review. I use it as much as I can (sometimes because it is helpful and sometimes just to learn how to use it even if it slows me down).  A BIG limitation is that my data is often sensitive, otherwise I would use it far more to assist with data analysis. I use both Claude and Purdue’s copilot and sometimes compare answers. I worry about my ideas being taken when using Claude which is why I also use Purdues copilot for certain things. I love LLMs for writing but find it enables me be a much better writer not necessarily save time ( since ultimately I end up going through  even more iterations of writing and possible organizations of the points). I specifically do not use LLMs when I want close qualitative review of quantitative patterns, or for peer review.  I do find that LLMs for thinking about quantitative data analysis slows me down considerably but in a good way: I learn about methods, checks, and limitations I wouldn’t have thought of and can implement considerably more robustness checks. I am very wary of using LLMs to implement methods I’m not already familiar with. Another limitation is that Claude, especially, is way too overconfident about its solutions or technical advice which can be frustrating and also misleading. I also use LLMs sometimes to get advice on my lesson plans and teaching materials (eg check for where my assignment descriptions might be unclear, and brainstorm new warm-up activities).  I wish I knew how to use AI more effectively ( eg for creating presentations, agents) and I feel pressure to use it more frequently and effectively as well so I stay current, but it also takes time to learn.
